message.content: Review my OrderService please, I want to learn from it.

content.content: class OrderService { public function send(Order $o): \Stripe\Charge { $pdf = new PdfRenderer(new Fonts(), 'A4'); $mail = new Mailer(new SmtpTransport('smtp.local')); ... return $this->billing->charge($o); } }

content.text: It works. send() renders a PDF, mails it and charges the order.

message.content: Two things I want you to explain to me and remember. First: send() builds PdfRenderer and Mailer itself, with new, and then uses them. Building objects and using them are different jobs. The building should be in a separate factory class and send() should get ready objects.

content.text: Right. I'll move construction into a factory and inject the renderer and mailer.

message.content: Second: Billing::charge() returns Stripe\Charge. Billing uses Stripe inside, fine, but it should return its own result type, a Billing result, not Stripe's class. Now everyone who calls Billing depends on Stripe too.

content.text: Understood. Billing will return a BillingResult and keep Stripe inside.
Done: OrderDocumentsFactory builds the renderer and mailer; Billing::charge() returns BillingResult.
